sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: pedestrians, school zones, bicycles, motorcycles, large vehicles, buses and special vehicles
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The extracted text of physical page fifty-seven repeats physical page fifty-six word for word (school zones, white canes and children at play); facts cite the earlier page only, and whether the printed page carries other content is held as debt [A03] (verify OR-SHARE-D-DUPPAGE).
The motorcycle page carries a helmet poster whose print-production text is not manual content and is ignored [A06].
The stopped-vehicle paragraph says you must change lanes and that you may also slow to a set margin under the posted limit; it does not say whether slowing replaces the lane change when a change is unsafe, so part C2 states it exactly as printed [A11] (verify OR-SHARE-D-MOVEOVER).
Crosswalk, bike box, school zone sign and stopped bus pictures are not in the extracted text; only their written captions and paragraphs are used.
No fines or fees appear in these pages; the school-hours window is the only time-variable value and it is stated as printed.

corpus_stability.reason: The Oregon Driver Manual is a two-year edition (the front cover names a two-year span and the back cover carries a single form revision code); fees and office details are sent to the DMV website rather than printed, and nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year.

verification_debt.claim_text: The extracted text of physical page 57 (printed page 49) is identical to physical page 56 (printed page 48). Confirm against the rendered PDF whether printed page 49 is a true duplicate or carries other content that the extraction missed.

Physical page 65 says drivers must change lanes when approaching a stopped vehicle with flashing lights on a multi-lane road and may also slow down by at least 5 mph under the posted limit; whether slowing is an alternative when a lane change is unsafe is not stated. Confirm against the Oregon statute before teaching the slow-down option as an alternative.
